title: Chang's version of Freiman's theorem and the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma
abstract: Formalization of Chang's version of Freiman's theorem, with a 2-proper progression P: a finite set X of integers with |X + X| <= kappa |X| is contained in a 2-proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most the Freiman dimension of X, hence at most 2 kappa - 1, with at most exp(10^32 kappa^7) |X| points. If kappa (2 kappa - 1) <= epsilon |X|, the dimension is at most floor(kappa - 1 + epsilon), as in Green and Tao. There is also a statement for subsets of ZMod q with q prime, where the progression has at most exp(10^30 kappa^7) |X| points. The bound on the size is weaker than that of Chang. The first step of the proof, the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, is stated too: if moreover |X| >= 7 * 10^7 kappa^2, then 2X - 2X contains a proper progression of dimension at most 3 * 10^5 kappa^2 with at least exp(-2 * 10^7 kappa^2) |X| points.
